series: Flagship #20 (SALES FIRST); week of Oct 12 theme: the rate that covers your unpaid hours; CMO slate Oct 12 am
hook: Bill half your hours and you need $89.58 an hour
hook_say: If clients pay for only half your hours, a $60,000 take-home needs $89.58 an hour.

rows.label: Take-home pay you want
rows.say: You want to take home $60,000 a year
rows.why: The calculator's example goal: $60,000 a year after tax and costs.

rows.label: Tax (25%) + business costs
rows.say: Add $26,000 for tax and business costs
rows.why: A 25% tax set-aside on the take-home is $20,000, plus $6,000 of yearly business costs.

rows.label: Money you must bring in
rows.why: $60,000 plus $20,000 of tax set-aside plus $6,000 of costs.

rows.label: Hours you work (48 wks x 40)
rows.why: 48 weeks of 40 hours. Admin, quotes, travel and email all count as work.

rows.label: Hours clients pay for (50%)
rows.say: Clients pay for half of them, 960 hours
rows.why: Type your own share. Here clients pay for 50% of the hours you work.

rows.label: Hourly rate you need
rows.why: $86,000 spread over 960 paid hours is $89.58 an hour.

fix.label: Rate needed if clients pay for 80%
fix.say: If clients pay for 80% of your hours, the rate you need drops to $55.99
fix.why: Same goal, tax and costs over 1,536 paid hours: $55.99 an hour. The calculator shows 50, 60, 70 and 80% side by side.

A $60,000 take-home goal, a 25% tax set-aside and $6,000 of yearly costs means bringing in $86,000. You work 1,920 hours a year, but if clients pay for only half of them, that is 960 paid hours: $89.58 an hour. Get clients to pay for 80% of your hours and the rate drops to $55.99. Example numbers from the Hourly Rate Quick Calculator; estimates, not tax advice.
